messages.text: I've got a new batch of matches queued. Two API services that keep calling each other—think they're meant to be.
Cute. But desire isn't enough. Are they stable? Do they handle rejection—I mean, timeouts—gracefully?
They retry with backoff and have circuit breakers. I ran a quick compatibility check. High affinity.
Then let them meet. I care about beauty in the contract—clear schemas, sensible defaults. If the handshake is ugly, the relationship won't last.
I'll nudge the teams to document the contract. You want to review the first few request/response samples?
Yes. And no optional fields that are actually required. That's the kind of seduction that ends in production tears.
Noted. I'm curious how they'll behave under load. Maybe we run a little chaos—see if they stay loyal.
Passion under stress is the real test. Set it up. I'll watch the metrics. If they're still talking nicely after that, we ship it.
Deal. Love and beauty, together again.
Just make sure the rollout is gradual. Even the best matches need a soft launch.
